newsitem.title: CROATIA: Creditanstalt says in Croat dairy deal.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt says in Croat dairy deal.

text.p: The Croatian investment unit of Austria's bank Creditanstalt (CAIB) said on Tuesday it was acting as an adviser in a deal designed to raise funds for expansion of leading Croatian dairy Dukat.
"Dukat needs to get an access to a new market. We support a strategic solution because money alone is not an answer," CAIB director Gabriel Dielacher told Reuters in an interview.
Croatian newspapers said the bank was rumoured to be interested in buying shares in the dairy, which is part of a private Lura group, owned by young tycoon Luka Rajic.
Dielacher confirmed CAIB had signed a letter of intent and might close the deal to buy into Dukat this month or in January.
He declined to reveal the size of the proposed purchase.
"It might not be a majority, depending on the final structure," he said, pointing out that the bank would not keep the shares in its own portfolio but aimed to resell the package in 1997.
It hoped to bring in a strategic investor, coupled with a financial institution. This would be a first step to floating the dairy shares abroad later, Dielacher said.
"Dukat is a good company and we feel it will be interesting to investors. It is a risk, but it's worth it," he added.
Dukat's equity is estimated at 65 million German marks, of which Lura has 85 percent and the rest is owned by small shareholders.
With majority stakes in two other dairies apart from Dukat, Lura controls some 70 percent of the Croatian market.
